reconstructed_theorem_text:
Let E be any real inner-product space with a measurable Borel structure and second-countable topology. For every real kappa>=1 and arbitrary measures mu,nu on phase space S=E x E,define
  Q_kappa(x,p)=(1/(2kappa)+1/2)||x||^2+<x,p>+||p||^2,
  C_kappa(s,sprime)=ENNReal.ofReal(Q_kappa(s-sprime)),
  P_kappa(mu,nu)=inf_{pi coupling of mu,nu} integral^- C_kappa(s,sprime) dpi.
Couplings are measures on S x S with first marginal mu and second marginal nu. Let the ordinary phase product norm be the default maximum norm,so for s=(x,p),sprime=(xprime,pprime),
  dmax(s,sprime)=max(||x-xprime||,||p-pprime||).
Define the ordinary quadratic transport cost cmax(s,sprime)=ENNReal.ofReal(dmax(s,sprime)^2),and let
  Wmax(mu,nu)=[inf_{pi coupling of mu,nu} integral^- cmax(s,sprime) dpi]^(1/2:R)
in extended nonnegative reals. This is precisely WassersteinSpace.wassersteinDistance for the stated product norm. Then
  Wmax(mu,nu)^2 <= ENNReal.ofReal(6) P_kappa(mu,nu).
The left side is the unrooted quadratic-cost coupling infimum,and P_kappa is phaseWassersteinSq,also unrooted,using the explicit tilted quadratic energy. The integral is the lower integral and the root is ENNReal real exponentiation. Both measures are arbitrary: no probability normalization,finite-moment,finite-mass or coupling-existence assumption is separately supplied. No completeness or finite-dimensionality assumption is stated. The theorem is one comparison of transport quantities,not a contraction theorem for any numerical map or a finiteness conclusion.
objects: Real-inner-product E with measurable Borel and second-countable structures;real kappa>=1;arbitrary phase measures mu,nu;explicit Q_kappa,ofReal phase cost C_kappa and unrooted phase coupling cost P_kappa;default maximum product norm and corresponding quadratic cost cmax;ordinary Wasserstein Wmax defined by the half real power of that coupling infimum.
domains: E is real-inner-product and has MeasurableSpace,BorelSpace,SecondCountableTopology. kappa in R;mu,nu are Measure(E x E). Couplings are measures on (E x E) x (E x E). Quadratic costs,infima,Wmax and its square are ENNReal values. The ordinary product norm is max(||x||,||p||),while Q is the explicit coordinate expression. No finite-dimensionality,completeness or probability typeclass is imposed.
quantifiers: For every E with those structures,every kappa>=1 and every pair of measures mu,nu,the transport inequality holds. Both cost definitions infimize over all couplings with their exact marginals. There is no existentially selected coupling,no optimality/attainment quantifier and no restriction to probability measures.
assumptions: kappa>=1;E real-inner-product,measurable Borel and second countable. mu,nu are arbitrary measures. The approved definitions supply Q,phaseCost,phaseWassersteinSq and ordinary wassersteinDistance as the half real power of quadraticCost transport. No finite-moment,finite-mass,probability normalization,coupling existence or nonlinear-map hypothesis is stated.
conclusion: WassersteinSpace.wassersteinDistance(mu,nu)^2<=ENNReal.ofReal(6)*phaseWassersteinSq(kappa,mu,nu),where the left distance uses maximum-product-norm quadratic cost and the right uses ofReal of the explicit tilted quadratic form.

The ordinary distance is based on quadratic cost with exponent 1/2,not an undefined-order API or a linear-distance cost. Its product norm is maximum rather than the Euclidean L2 product norm. The right quantity stores the square directly. No probability normalization,actual sampler history,nonlinear update or iterative contraction is included.
